newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong newspaper headlines-May 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong newspaper headlines-May 13.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- MING PAO -- Political reform will be a fixture of the 15th general conference of the Chinese Communist Party. The reforms will focus on strengthening the party's internal supervision and the role of the legislative National People's Congress, and would establish a checks-and-balance system.

-- APPLE DAILY -- Because mainland gangsters were being watched by Macau police, triads in the Portuguese-run enclave were planning to hire killers from Thailand to push ahead with a gang war that has left at least 14 people dead since the start of the year.
-- WEN WEI PO -- In an interview with French media, Chinese President Jiang Zemin said China's "one country, two systems" principle would be used to resolve the Taiwan issue.
-- China successfully launched a domestic telecommunications satellite atop a Long March 3A rocket.

-- TIN TIN DAILY -- A "China Human Rights Party" would be set up in Hong Kong by overseas human rights activists, with the aim of putting an end to one-party rule in China and eventually becoming a ruling party in the country.
-- ECONOMIC TIMES -- The share price of fashion retailer Giordano went up 11 percent on rumours some China-backed investors had been buying its stock.

-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- Post-handover leader Tung Chee-hwa plans to reject calls to ban mainland donations to local political parties because Hong Kong and China will be "one country" as of July 1.

-- HONGKONG STANDARD -- Hong Kong Monetary Authority chief executive Joseph Yam challenged the Asia Development Bank to look beyond its traditional role of financing development projects. Yam said the bank should help member countries to develop their own financial sectors.
-- Hong Kong Electric Holdings said it was hoping to finalise its first ever foray outside Hong Kong by September.
